column1: # One row per case, five tab-separated columns — see tests/README.md.
#   fixture   the envelope drive.sh builds the fake account from, or `-` for a call refused
#             before the login shell or any stub runs
#   args      batch-launch.mjs's arguments; a NAME=value word goes to the environment
#   exit      0 an answer, 2 a call the script cannot act on
#   expect    `|`-separated fragments of the compacted answer; `NOT:` must be absent

column5: outside agterm no terminal mode answers, and claude and aimux are the ones the LOGIN shell's PATH holds — never this session's own PATH, which carries a real claude
a profile that prints a greeting and a PATH= line before the environment does not become the environment
a login that fails is an unread environment, said with its status — never an environment with nothing on it

column4: mode:null|claude is not on the login shell|aimux is not on the login shell
column5: agterm answers, but nothing to run a batch with is on the login PATH, so neither terminal mode does
the session is found in the window it moved to — the window id it was spawned with names another — and both terminal modes answer

column4: agtermctl version: agtermctl: could not connect|"mode":null
column5: the variables alone do not make agterm answer: a socket that does not answer is no terminal mode
a socket that answers for some other agterm session is not this session's terminal
absent from the windows that were read is not absent: one window's tree did not answer, so where this session stands is unread
an aimux whose core lost a function is aimux unread, never aimux with no limits — and the plain terminal mode still answers

column4: profile:"p","fiveHourPct":0,"weeklyPct":0,"eligible":true,"login":"ok","warmed":true|aimux run p auth status --json|aimux run p -m haiku -- . -p
column5: a profile whose login does not answer but is logged in is warmed, and its limits read again
a profile that is not logged in is the user's to log into: no warm-up request is spent on it
a window exactly at its ceiling is over it, the five-hour and the weekly alike
room is divided by the batches a profile already carries, this session's own profile counting one: the freer profile is not the pick
a batch the master already runs on a profile counts against it
a probe that throws leaves that profile unread, never eligible

column5: with no profile to put a batch on, the aimux mode does not answer and the plain one does
only the allowed profiles are read, and a name aimux does not know is said rather than dropped
a setting the user never saved arrives as its literal placeholder, and the manifest's default stands in
the user's word outranks the saved setting, which outranks the default
